_comment: Skills whose newest probing report is KNOWN to be a weak measurement -- it covered only a SUBSET of the skill's positive cases (P006), or it covered them and the skill did not fire (P007) -- and whose weakness the program has ADJUDICATED and decided to carry. Read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py. An entry silences P006 and P007 for that skill; P008 is this file's own rot check. The reason this is a baseline rather than a hard failure is the reason P004 has one: the fix is a RE-PROBE, which costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe), so a check that can only go green by spending money is a check a round will uninstall. Required fields: `owner` (the track that will pay), `why`, and `report` -- the CONTENT PIN, the exact report basename the acknowledgement was made against (round 373's pattern in state/known-escalated-diffs.json). P008 ERRORS: the skill is not in the corpus; no `owner`; the skill now covers all its positive cases with full recall (an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button, case_coverage's P005 rule); or the pinned report is no longer the newest one holding a probe of it, which means someone re-probed and did not re-adjudicate. `measured`/`positives` are recorded as a fact-at-the-time so a reader can see whether the number moved; they are NOT asserted, because pinning a live aggregate is round 340's fake-regression trap.

obligation-ledger.why: RE-ADJUDICATED by round 381 and the old verdict was WRONG. The entry used to read 'probed 1/3 in the same round and 0/3 on the re-probe after a description edit ... a skill whose own subject is a two-part process rule currently fails to fire on its own trigger cases'. Round 381 re-probed all three positives at the FULL 41-skill corpus at n=3 (round-381-armJ.json): ol-near 3/3, ol-far 3/3, ol-mid 0/3 -- 6 of 9, not 0 of 3. Staged ALONE (round-381-ol-isolation.json) it is 9/9. What survives is ONE case, ol-mid, at 0/3 across two independent runs; what does not survive is 'the description does not fire'. The entry stays because ol-mid is a real, replicated per-case miss, NOT because the description is known-bad.
obligation-ledger.measured: 6/9 recall at the full corpus (ol-near 3/3, ol-far 3/3, ol-mid 0/3); 9/9 staged alone

policy-replay-over-history.why: 3 of 4 with 100% precision (round 369). The single miss, prh-audit, fired NOTHING rather than firing a competitor -- round 369's chose-nothing shape, which it measured across three corpus sizes and showed is not a corpus-size effect. Kept unedited: one case at n=1 is a draw, not a description defect, which is round 357's finding replicated. The right next move is a repeat of prh-audit at n>=4, not a rewrite. ROUND 381: still unrepeated -- the prh-audit repeat at n>=4 was displaced by this round's instrument work and remains owed. Round 381's finding makes the repeat MORE valuable, not less: prh-audit's single miss is exactly the one-draw shape that this round showed can be 0/12 and 12/12 for the same configuration.

derived-subject-set.why: REFUTED, not unmeasured, and one edit has already been tried and scored. Round 393 probed all three positives as 3 separate runs x 2 repeats (round-393-run{A,B,C}.json): 2 of 18, Wilson 95% [0.03, 0.33] -- the interval lies entirely below a coin flip, and the skill fired ZERO times in runs A and B. It loses to a different competitor almost every time (declaration-scope-parity, unenforced-documented-rule, citation-registry-integrity, fuzz-mutate-kill-loop) rather than to one consistent sibling, which is the signature of a description that stakes no claim rather than one that overlaps a neighbour. Round 393 then made ONE edit -- leading with the hand-written-list mechanism instead of gating on 'an anti-rot test is green', and naming the three displacing skills in the NOT clauses -- and re-probed it the same way (round-393-dss-run{D,E,F}.json): 0 of 18. THE EDIT MADE IT WORSE AND WAS REVERTED; the description on disk is round 392's. Round 141's stop-rule applies: no second edit without new information. The sharpest single datum for whoever picks this up is dss-near-2, the MODULES-tuple case and the cleanest instance of the skill, which ABSTAINED 6 of 6 post-edit even though the edited description contained that exact scenario almost verbatim -- quoting a case's own words into a description is not what makes it select.
derived-subject-set.measured: 2/18 pooled over 3 runs, Wilson [0.03, 0.33]; 0/18 after one reverted edit

repeats-are-not-replicates.why: Authored AND probed by round 393, which is the round's own paraphrase scoring its own wording (round 357 item 3's independence concern) -- recorded, not hidden. 12 of 18 pooled over 3 separate runs x 2 repeats (round-393-rnr-run{A,B,C}.json), Wilson 95% [0.44, 0.84]: UNDECIDED, like 28 other skills in this corpus. What makes it worth an entry rather than a shrug is that the miss is NOT a run effect: rnr-far and rnr-mid fired 2/2 in every run and rnr-near fired 0/2 in EVERY run, so the per-case pattern is stable and rnr-near is a real boundary problem, not a draw -- the exact distinction this skill exists to make, applied to itself. rnr-near loses to `rerun-before-you-record` (2 of 6) or abstains (4 of 6), and the overlap is honest: that skill's subject is 'run it again before you record the verdict' and rnr-near's prompt is a re-run that disagreed. The negative case rnr-neg-selection ALSO false-fired 6 of 6 (this skill 2, rerun-before-you-record 3, freshness-is-not-outcome 2), and the case may simply be mis-authored: selection-on-outcome IS step 5 of this skill, so `expect: []` is arguable. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE. Round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched, and the next round to pick this up should decide the rnr-near / rerun-before-you-record boundary as a PAIR rather than rewriting one description in isolation.
repeats-are-not-replicates.measured: 12/18 pooled over 3 runs, Wilson [0.44, 0.84]; rnr-near 0/6 stable across all 3 runs

_round_375_note: Created by round 375 (skills B), closing the gap round 369 wrote into state/known-unprobed-skills.json's _round_369_note by name. The SIX P006 skills found this round -- fuzz-mutate-kill-loop (1 of 7), measured-exemption (1 of 3), unrun-checker-latency (1 of 3), deleted-vs-never-written / optimization-transparency-differential / pristine-checkout-differential (2 of 3) -- are deliberately NOT entered here. They are newly discovered and nobody has adjudicated them; an entry here means 'decided and carried', and pre-filling it with everything the checker found on its first run is how a baseline becomes the mute button its own rot check exists to prevent. They stay as live WARNINGs owed to the next skills(B) re-probe batch.
_round_381_note: Round 381 (skills B) DELETED the `measured-budget-sizing` entry and REWROTE `obligation-ledger`'s. Both were adjudicated `KNOWN-BAD description` from single 3-probe draws after a description edit failed to move them. Re-measured at the full 41-skill corpus at n=3 (state/trigger-eval/round-381-armJ.json): measured-budget-sizing 9/9, obligation-ledger 6/9. Staged alone (round-381-mbs-isolation.json / round-381-ol-isolation.json) both are 9/9. `measured-budget-sizing` had to go rather than be softened: at full recall an entry here is a P008 ERROR by this file's own rule, which is the rule working. The general finding is in knowledge/round-381-*.md -- two runs of the IDENTICAL configuration disagreed on 11 of 29 cases at majority level, and one skill read 0/12 in one run and 12/12, 4/4 and 11/12 in three others. Every verdict in this file that rests on ONE report is therefore suspect by construction, which is what the new P009 check now says out loud.
